scope: Theorem 6.6 (Existence on finite truncations) of the manuscript “Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Boundary-graph-deformations-for-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 49-50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the prepared domain of Proposition 3.7 and every sufficiently small fixed ϵ > 0, there is an integer N0 ≥ 4 and, for each N ≥ N0, a radius 49 Rmin(N), with Rmin(N) → ∞, such that the original deformation system has a smooth solution on every ΩR with R ≥ Rmin(N). It satisfies t > −ϵ on the closure. At fixed N, these solutions have the local bounds of Proposition 6.3, uniformly as R → ∞. In particular, any sequence Rj → ∞ of such radii has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of Ω to a solution of the original equations with t ≥ −ϵ.
